candidates.name: sodapy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for the Socrata Open Data API. NYC Open Data (data.cityofnewyork.us), LA (data.lacity.org / MyLA311), and San Francisco (datasf.org) all run on Socrata, so this client is the direct mechanism for pulling the NYC 311 Service Requests dataset (Socrata id erm2-nwe9, filterable to complaint types like 'Illegal Vacation Rental Unit', 'Short-Term Rental', 'Illegal Conversion / Illegal Hotel Rental'), LA's MyLA311 service request dataset, and SF 311 Cases, on a point-in-time basis (SoQL supports as_of-style filtering by created_date). No data committed in the repo itself — it is the pull mechanism, not a mirror.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery/pull clients) and is the concrete tool to build the exact 311-Airbnb-mention enforcement/activity proxy this theme is scoped around — NYC, LA and SF 311 STR/illegal-hotel complaint volume as a monthly panel, refreshable and point-in-time by created_date.
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained historically; not independently re-verified this run (search access blocked)
candidates.geography: US cities on Socrata (NYC, LA, SF, and others)

candidates.name: ckanapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Command-line tool and Python client for the CKAN open-data API, used by many municipal and national open-data portals (some EU cities' STR registries, e.g. Amsterdam/Barcelona portals, run CKAN rather than Socrata).
candidates.why_useful: Complements sodapy for gap #17 — lets an agent discover and pull STR/complaint datasets from CKAN-based city portals outside the Socrata set (useful for the EU registration/enforcement trackers in gap #12), rounding out a cross-city 311/enforcement-proxy pull pipeline.
candidates.last_activity: not independently re-verified this run (search access blocked)

notes: This theme hit a wall of rate limits rather than a wall of empty results. Every `gh search repos` call for 311/Airbnb/noise-complaint/enforcement terms ('311 airbnb complaints', 'nyc 311 short term rental', '311 complaints airbnb', '311 short term rental', 'MyLA311 short term rental', 'airbnb noise complaints', 'illegal hotel nyc 311', 'short-term rental enforcement') returned either an empty array or, after the shared search-API quota was exhausted by other concurrent scouts, HTTP 403 'API rate limit exceeded'. The two non-403 queries that did return ('nyc 311 short term rental', 'MyLA311 short term rental', 'airbnb noise complaints', 'illegal hotel nyc 311', 'short-term rental enforcement') came back genuinely empty ([]) — gh search repos' full-text matching on repo name/description/README is narrow and these multi-word city-agency-specific phrases apparently don't hit any indexed repo. Fallback channels were also blocked in sequence: this session's WebSearch quota (200/200) was already exhausted before this scout ran (used by earlier scouts on the same shared session), a direct WebFetch to github.com/search returned HTTP 429 with a 3600s Retry-After (github.com itself is being hammered by the other ~10 concurrent scouts), and duckduckgo.com/html returned HTTP 403. Bing search via WebFetch loaded but the rendered page did not surface actual repo result links (only chrome/nav elements), so it could not confirm or deny candidates either. Net effect: I cannot rule out that a real committed-data repo for NYC/LA/SF 311-Airbnb complaints exists on GitHub — I simply could not reach a working search surface to find it this run. The two candidates I did report (sodapy, ckanapi) are recalled from general knowledge as real, well-known, actively-used API clients (not verified live this session) that are the correct *mechanism* for this exact theme (pulling NYC/LA/SF 311 short-term-rental/illegal-hotel complaint series from their Socrata backends) even though no committed dataset was found. Recommend a re-run of this theme once the shared gh search-API and github.com scraping quotas reset (~1 hour), trying narrower single-word queries (e.g. 'airbnb311', '311nyc', 'illegalhotel') and `gh search repos --topic=nyc-311` / `--topic=open-data-nyc`, plus a direct check of whether NYC's Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement (OSE) illegal-hotel dataset (already flagged as held, per CONTEXT.md municipal STR registries) has any GitHub mirror with a longer back-history than what NYC Open Data currently serves.
